# 2 Baruch Chapter 32 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**1** Everything that exists now amounts to nothing. What is coming will be great. All that is perishable will pass away; everything that dies will go. The present time itself will be forgotten — no one will remember this age — because what is coming is coming quickly.

**2** The souls of the righteous who are suffering right now — they know what has been prepared for them, and that knowledge keeps them from despair.

**3** As for us — if we didn't know we were in distress, we would understand nothing. But we do know that the world's suffering will not last.

**4** I said to them further: "Won't all these troubles pass from us? Won't a time of rest finally come? Look — Zion will be rebuilt, the sacrifices will be restored, the priests will return to their service, and the people will come back to the land."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. The present-versus-coming contrast is vivid and urgent. The promise of Zion's rebuilding (v.4) provides concrete hope for the immediate future, while the larger eschatological hope looms in the background.*
